title: 戴维宁等效：量开路电压和短路电流
summary: 一个电源和三个电阻组成的网络，从两个端子看出去，只需要两个数就能描述：开路电压和短路电流。
concepts: open-circuit voltage 开路电压 Uoc
short-circuit current 短路电流 Isc
description: 戴维宁定理：任何线性二端网络，对外都等效于一个电压源 V_Th 串联一个电阻 R_Th。V_Th 是开路电压，R_Th = 开路电压 ÷ 短路电流，也可以把电源置零后从端口看进去求。

cards.title: 两个数，认出一个盒子
text: 照目标电路图搭：`9 V` → **R1** → 结点 **A**；**R2** 从 A 到 GND；**R3** 从 A 到端子 **T**。
从 T 出发，按键 **SW1** 和电流表 **AM1** 通到 GND：按下按键，就是经过电流表把 T 短接到 GND。
**松开按键**：测 T 对 GND 的电压。**按住按键**：读 AM1。
假装看不到盒子里面。这两个数能告诉你什么？

cards.title: 每个网络都是一节“带内阻的电池”
text: - 在 1.10 里，电池 = 一个电压加一个小内阻。**戴维宁定理**：任何由电源和电阻组成的网络，从两个端子看出去，都正好是这样。
![](fig:equiv)
- $V_{Th}$ 就是什么都不接时的电压（开路电压 $V_{oc}$）。把端子短接，只剩 $R_{Th}$ 限制电流，所以：
$$R_{Th} = \frac{V_{oc}}{I_{sc}}$$
- 拿 9 V 电池试试：$V_{oc} = 9$ V，$I_{sc} = 6$ A，$R_{Th} = 9 / 6 = 1.5$ Ω——正是电池的内阻。
- 第二种算法，不用表：把电源置零（9 V → 导线），从 T 看进去。这时 R1 和 R2 并联，再和 R3 串联。
![](fig:lookin)

cards.title: 开路一次，短路一次
text: - **松开按键**：万用表红表笔点 **T**，黑表笔接 GND。这就是 $V_{oc}$。
- **按住按键**：读 **AM1**。电流表只有 0.1 Ω，这就是 $I_{sc}$。
- 电路检查通过后填测量题；最后一题用你自己的两个读数相除。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **戴维宁**：从两个端子看，任何线性网络 = $V_{Th}$ 串 $R_{Th}$。
- 求 $R_{Th}$ 两种方法：实验台上 $V_{oc}/I_{sc}$；纸上把电源置零、从端口看进去。两者一致。
- 坑：短路电流法只适合 $I_{sc}$ 很小的网络，比如这一个。**千万不要直接短路电池或电源的输出**去“测”它。
- 真实万用表 mA 档有几欧的负担电阻，测得的 $I_{sc}$ 会小约 1%。
- 下一步：什么样的负载能从这个盒子里拿到最多的功率？

caption.text: 从 T 和 GND 看进去，整个网络可以换成一个电压源 V_Th 串一个电阻 R_Th。

i18n.en: Seen from T and GND, the whole network can be replaced by one voltage source V_Th in series with one resistor R_Th.

caption.text: 电源置零：9 V 换成导线。从 T 看进去，R1 和 R2 并联，再串上 R3。

i18n.en: Sources off: the 9 V becomes a wire. Looking in from T, R1 and R2 are in parallel, then in series with R3.

en.title: Thévenin equivalent: measure the open-circuit voltage and the short-circuit current
en.summary: A network of one source and three resistors needs only two numbers to describe it from its two terminals: the open-circuit voltage and the short-circuit current.
en.description: Thévenin's theorem: any linear two-terminal network looks, from outside, like a voltage source V_Th in series with a resistor R_Th. V_Th is the open-circuit voltage; R_Th = open-circuit voltage ÷ short-circuit current, or the resistance seen from the terminals with the sources turned off.
en.compare: **Compare**: Voc = 9 × 2.2 / 3.2 ≈ **6.19 V**; simulator Isc ≈ **5.34 mA**; R_Th = 6.19 V / 5.345 mA ≈ **1158 Ω**. Sources off: R3 + (R1 ∥ R2) = 470 + 687.5 = 1157.5 Ω ✔. From outside the network is "6.19 V in series with 1.16 kΩ"; the next lab uses it to find the maximum power.

measurements.ask: Button released: open-circuit voltage Voc (multimeter, T to GND)
measurements.explain: With T open no current flows in R3, so T sits at A's voltage: Voc = 9 × 2.2 / 3.2 ≈ 6.19 V.

measurements.ask: Button held: short-circuit current Isc (AM1 reading)
measurements.explain: Isc = Voc / R_Th ≈ 6.19 V / 1158 Ω ≈ 5.34 mA.

measurements.ask: From your own two readings, the equivalent resistance R_Th = Voc / Isc
measurements.explain: Sources off: R3 + R1 ∥ R2 = 470 + 687.5 = 1157.5 Ω. The measured value is within 1 %, so both methods give the same R_Th.

hints: The button straddles the trench: one side to T (R3's far end), the other to the ammeter's red lead.
The ammeter's black lead goes to GND.
With the button released, the multimeter reading from T to GND is the open-circuit voltage.
tests: Released: port open, the ammeter reads 0

cards.title: Two numbers to know a box
text: Build it from the target schematic: `9 V` → **R1** → node **A**; **R2** from A to GND; **R3** from A to the terminal **T**.
From T, the button **SW1** and the ammeter **AM1** lead to GND: pressing the button shorts T to GND through the meter.
**Button released**: measure T to GND. **Button held**: read AM1.
Pretend you can't see inside. What do these two numbers tell you about the box?

cards.title: Every network is a battery with internal resistance
text: - In 1.10 a battery was a voltage plus a small internal resistance. **Thévenin's theorem**: any network of sources and resistors looks exactly like that from two terminals.
![](fig:equiv)
- $V_{Th}$ is the voltage with nothing connected (open circuit, $V_{oc}$). Shorting the terminals, only $R_{Th}$ limits the current, so:
$$R_{Th} = \frac{V_{oc}}{I_{sc}}$$
- Check it on a 9 V battery: $V_{oc} = 9$ V, $I_{sc} = 6$ A, so $R_{Th} = 9 / 6 = 1.5$ Ω — the battery's internal resistance.
- Second way, no meter needed: turn the source off (9 V → a wire) and look into T. R1 and R2 are then in parallel, in series with R3.
![](fig:lookin)

cards.title: Open once, short once
text: - **Button released**: multimeter red lead on **T**, black lead on GND. That is $V_{oc}$.
- **Button held**: read **AM1**. The meter is only 0.1 Ω, so this is $I_{sc}$.
- Once the circuit check passes, fill in the questions; the last one divides your own two readings.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Thévenin**: from two terminals, any linear network = $V_{Th}$ in series with $R_{Th}$.
- Two ways to $R_{Th}$: $V_{oc}/I_{sc}$ on the bench, or sources off and look in on paper. They agree.
- Pitfall: the short-circuit test only suits networks with a small $I_{sc}$, like this one. **Never short a battery or a supply output** to "measure" it.
- A real mA range adds a few ohms, so the measured $I_{sc}$ comes out about 1 % low.
- Next: what load gets the most power out of this box?

tests.name: 松开：端口开路，电流表读 0
按下：端口短路，端口电压 ≈ 0

measurements.ask: 按键松开：开路电压 Voc（万用表测 T 对 GND）
measurements.explain: 端口开路时 R3 里没有电流，T 和 A 一样高：Voc = 9 × 2.2 / 3.2 ≈ 6.19 V。

measurements.ask: 按住按键：短路电流 Isc（AM1 的读数）
measurements.explain: Isc = Voc / R_Th ≈ 6.19 V / 1158 Ω ≈ 5.34 mA。

measurements.ask: 用你自己的两个读数算等效电阻 R_Th = Voc / Isc
measurements.explain: 置零法：R3 + R1 ∥ R2 = 470 + 687.5 = 1157.5 Ω。测量值和它相差 1% 以内，说明两种方法得到的是同一个 R_Th。

hints: 按键横跨凹槽：一边接 T（R3 的另一端），另一边接电流表的红表笔。
松开按键时，用万用表测 T 对 GND 的电压，就是开路电压。
